Component mismatch: This check references 'slotted_freezable mechanism for Header objects' which appears to be Python-specific (likely ethereum/execution-specs). The Nethermind codebase is C# and uses a different BlockHeader class structure without a slotted_freezable pattern. The C# BlockHeader class at src/Nethermind/Nethermind.Core/BlockHeader.cs does not implement freeze() or __slots__.

phase1_analysis.notes: C# does not use Python's slotted_freezable pattern. BlockHeader is a mutable class with no freeze mechanism.

phase1_analysis.relevant_code: HeaderValidator.Validate() at lines 84-103 validates: FieldLimit, Hash, ExtraData, Parent, TotalDifficulty, Seal, GasUsed, GasLimit, Timestamp, BlockNumber, 1559 (BaseFeePerGas), BlobGasFields, RequestsHash
phase1_analysis.potential_gaps: Header.Bloom validation happens in BlockValidator.ValidateProcessedBlock (line 175) comparing computed vs suggested. StateRoot and ReceiptsRoot also validated there. TxRoot validated in ValidateTxRootMatchesTxs.

phase2_assessment.finding: Header field validation is comprehensive but split across HeaderValidator and BlockValidator. All 21 conceptual fields appear to be validated either directly or via hash comparison during processed block validation.

phase3_formal_audit.rationale: The validation is implemented correctly. HeaderValidator validates pre-execution fields (lines 84-103), while BlockValidator.ValidateProcessedBlock validates post-execution fields (Bloom, StateRoot, ReceiptsRoot) by hash comparison (lines 160-214). The header hash itself encodes all fields, so the hash check provides comprehensive validation.

phase1_analysis.relevant_code: Validate1559() at lines 128-143: UInt256? expectedBaseFee = BaseFeeCalculator.Calculate(parent, spec); if (expectedBaseFee != header.BaseFeePerGas) return false

phase2_assessment.finding: base_fee_per_gas is independently recomputed via BaseFeeCalculator.Calculate(parent, spec) and compared against header.BaseFeePerGas. The validation returns false if they don't match.

phase3_formal_audit.rationale: EIP-1559 base fee validation is correctly implemented. BaseFeeCalculator.Calculate() computes the expected base fee from parent block parameters per EIP-1559 formula. Line 134 performs exact comparison. Invalid base fees are rejected with appropriate error message.

phase1_analysis.relevant_code: ValidateBlobGasFields() validates: BlobGasUsed not null (line 340-344), ExcessBlobGas not null (line 347-352), ExcessBlobGas == BlobGasCalculator.CalculateExcessBlobGas(parentHeader, spec) (lines 354-360)

phase2_assessment.finding: Blob gas fields are validated when EIP-4844 is enabled. ExcessBlobGas is recomputed and compared. BlobGasUsed is validated in BlockValidator.ValidateEip4844Fields (lines 334-348) by counting blobs in transactions.

phase3_formal_audit.rationale: EIP-4844 blob gas validation is correctly implemented. HeaderValidator checks ExcessBlobGas computation (line 354-360). BlockValidator.ValidateEip4844Fields (lines 293-352) recomputes BlobGasUsed from transaction blob counts (line 334) and compares to header value (lines 343-348). Both values are independently verified.

phase1_analysis.relevant_code: ValidateRequestsHash() at lines 105-126: When spec.RequestsEnabled, checks header.RequestsHash is not null. When disabled, checks it is null.

phase2_assessment.finding: RequestsHash presence/absence is validated based on spec. However, the actual hash VALUE is validated in BlockValidator.ValidateProcessedBlock (lines 211-215) by comparing processedBlock.Header.RequestsHash != suggestedBlock.Header.RequestsHash.

phase3_formal_audit.rationale: EIP-7685 requests_hash validation is correctly implemented. HeaderValidator checks field presence (lines 105-126). BlockValidator.ValidateProcessedBlock validates the actual hash value by comparing computed vs suggested (lines 211-215). The requests_hash is computed during block processing and verified against the header.

phase1_analysis.relevant_code: Lines 92-97: spec.MaximumUncleCount check. Lines 99-104: ValidateUnclesHashMatches. Lines 106-111: _unclesValidator.Validate

phase2_assessment.finding: Uncle validation checks: (1) uncle count <= spec.MaximumUncleCount, (2) uncles hash matches, (3) uncles validator validates. Post-merge, MaximumUncleCount should be 0 per EIP-3675.

phase3_formal_audit.rationale: Post-merge ommer rejection is correctly enforced. The spec.MaximumUncleCount is 0 for post-merge blocks. Line 92-97 rejects blocks with uncles when count exceeds limit. Additionally, uncles hash is validated (lines 99-104) and uncle content validated (lines 106-111). Non-empty ommers in post-merge blocks are rejected.

phase1_analysis.relevant_code: Address property is typed as Address (20-byte type). AmountInGwei is ulong. AmountInWei computes AmountInGwei * 1.GWei() returning UInt256.

phase2_assessment.finding: Type safety is enforced by C# type system. Address is a 20-byte wrapper type. Amount is ulong (for GWei) or computed as UInt256 (for Wei).

phase3_formal_audit.rationale: Withdrawal address and amount are type-validated by C# strong typing. Address class ensures 20-byte addresses. ulong AmountInGwei prevents overflow for reasonable values. UInt256 AmountInWei handles larger values correctly. Deserialization validates types implicitly.

phase1_analysis.relevant_code: BitLength = 2048 (line 21), ByteLength = 256 (line 22). BloomData is InlineArray(256) (line 258). Bytes property returns _bloomData.AsSpan() of fixed 256 bytes.

phase2_assessment.finding: Bloom bytearray is always exactly 256 bytes via InlineArray(256) struct. No allocation or resizing possible. Access is through Span<byte> of fixed size.

phase3_formal_audit.rationale: Bloom filter is always exactly 256 bytes. The BloomData struct (line 258-264) uses C# InlineArray(ByteLength=256) which guarantees fixed-size inline storage. The Bytes property (line 56) returns a span over this fixed buffer. Out-of-bounds access is prevented by span bounds checking.

phase2_assessment.finding: The 0x07FF mask (11 bits = 2047) is correctly applied. Result is subtracted from 2047 giving range [0, 2047].

phase3_formal_audit.rationale: The 11-bit mask 0x07FF is correctly applied in BloomExtract (lines 242-244). The mask ensures the extracted value is in [0, 2047]. Subtracting from 2047 maintains this range. This matches the Ethereum Yellow Paper bloom filter specification.

phase1_analysis.relevant_code: WordMask (lines 202-213): wordIndex = bitIndex >> 6 (divide by 64). Given bitIndex in [0,2047], wordIndex is in [0,31]. Bloom has 32 ulongs = 256 bytes = 2048 bits.

phase2_assessment.finding: byte_index computation: bitIndex >> 6 gives [0,31] for ulong word index. This corresponds to byte indices [0,255] when accessing the underlying bytes. The computation is correct.

phase3_formal_audit.rationale: The byte/word index computation is correct. WordMask (lines 202-213) computes wordIndex = bitIndex >> 6, which for bitIndex in [0,2047] gives wordIndex in [0,31]. ULongs array has 32 elements (256 bytes / 8). All accesses are within bounds.

phase1_analysis.relevant_code: GetExtract (lines 225-238) computes Keccak hash, reads first 8 bytes as ulong, constructs BloomExtract. BloomExtract extracts 3 indices from positions 48, 32, 16 (2-byte pairs).

phase2_assessment.finding: Iteration reads 3 x 2-byte pairs at bit positions 48, 32, 16 from the first 8 bytes of Keccak hash. This matches the Yellow Paper specification for 3 index extractions.

phase3_formal_audit.rationale: Bloom index extraction correctly reads exactly 3 x 2-byte pairs. GetExtract (lines 225-238) computes Keccak hash and reads first 8 bytes as ulong. BloomExtract (lines 240-247) extracts 3 indices at bit offsets 48, 32, 16 (each 16-bit/2-byte pair). This matches Ethereum Yellow Paper bloom filter specification.

phase1_analysis.relevant_code: Default constructor Bloom() (line 25) creates BloomData struct which is zero-initialized by C# value type semantics. BloomData uses InlineArray with byte _element0.

phase2_assessment.finding: Bloom filter is initialized to 256 zero bytes. BloomData is a struct (value type) initialized to zeros by CLR. InlineArray ensures contiguous zero memory.

phase3_formal_audit.rationale: Bloom filter is correctly initialized to 256 zero bytes. BloomData (lines 259-264) is a struct using InlineArray(256). C# value type semantics guarantee zero-initialization of all bytes. New Bloom() (line 25) uses default struct initialization. Empty singleton (line 20) is never modified (line 61-64 throws if attempted).

phase1_analysis.relevant_code: Add(LogEntry[] logEntries) at lines 117-131: For each log entry, calls Set(addressBytes) then for each topic calls Set(topic.Bytes).

phase2_assessment.finding: Every log address is added exactly once per log entry (line 123). Loop iterates all entries (line 119), processes address first (line 122-123).

phase3_formal_audit.rationale: Every log address is added to bloom exactly once. Add() (lines 117-131) iterates logEntries (line 119), for each entry gets addressBytes (line 122) and calls Set(addressBytes) exactly once (line 123). No address is skipped or duplicated.

phase1_analysis.relevant_code: Add(LogEntry[] logEntries) lines 124-129: Hash256[] topics = logEntry.Topics; for (int topicIndex = 0; topicIndex < topics.Length; topicIndex++) { Set(topics[topicIndex].Bytes); }

phase2_assessment.finding: Every log topic is added exactly once. Inner loop (lines 125-129) iterates all topics and calls Set() for each. Total add_to_bloom calls per log = 1 (address) + topics.Length.

phase3_formal_audit.rationale: Every log topic is added to bloom exactly once. Add() (lines 117-131) iterates through topics array (lines 124-129), calling Set(topic.Bytes) for each topic. Total Set() calls per log entry = 1 (address) + len(topics), which matches the specification.
